div.p: Version 6.0 - Updated August 26, 2026 - PremaFirm Logistics

Prema Dispatch is a scheduled shared-LTL freight management system for the Ontario–Quebec corridor. It handles every step from customer booking through dispatch execution, load planning, GPS tracking, POD collection, invoicing, and accounting.

Everything centers on the Booking (logistics.booking). Whether a shipment comes in by phone, customer portal, WhatsApp, an existing invoice, a custom quote, or a recurring agreement — it always becomes one Booking with its own stops, freight lines, operational legs, tax decision, invoice, and dispatch job.

tr.td: Customer sends load tender via WA

p.b: Booking → Stops → Lines → Legs → Tax → Invoice → Dispatch Job → Load Plan → Driver Worksheet → Pickup → Transit → Delivery → POD → Accounting

div.p: Click Prema Dispatch in the top navigation bar. The default page is the Live Fleet Map showing all operational trucks with GPS positions. The sidebar menu is organized into:

ul.li: Dispatch Operations — Live Map, Booking Board, Dispatch Planner, Load Plans, Driver Worksheets, Find Available Truck
Bookings — All Bookings, Phone Booking, Internal Booking, Recurring Agreements, Custom Quotes, WhatsApp Negotiations
Network — Where We Go, Service Routes (Corridors), Departures, Regions, FSAs, Cities, Saved Locations, Carriers, Carrier Lane Rates, Carrier Offers, Execution Scenarios
Fleet — Trucks, Drivers, Equipment Profiles, GeoTab Settings
Reports — All Jobs, Completed, Stops, Freight Items, LTL Consolidations, On-Time %, Lane Profitability, Fuel Efficiency, POD Aging
User Manual — This page
Settings — Stages and system configuration

div.div: Rate Plans and technical lanes are historical only and are removed from normal navigation.

div.h3: Setting Up a Customer for Booking

ol.li: Open Contacts and create or select the customer
Under Sales & Purchase: set Logistics Pricing Status to Approved
Under Freight Tax Profile: set Billing Relationship (Direct Shipper / Interlining Carrier / Manual Review)
Set Tax Treatment (Automatic / Zero-Rated / Manual Review)

div.div: Billing Relationship determines how tax is applied. Direct Shippers get destination-based HST/GST. Interlining Carriers get zero-rated tax. Manual Review flags every booking for accountant review.
div.p: To make a contact usable as a driver: check Is Driver on the contact form. This enables the Driver App login and driver assignment on dispatch jobs.
Navigate: Network → Saved Locations
Saved Locations are the canonical address book for pickups and deliveries. Each location stores:

ul.li: Address, Google Place ID, GPS coordinates
Entrance/dock/parking/gate photos
Dock height, liftgate availability, truck accessibility
Visit statistics (average wait, unload times)
Duplicate detection (same address + same company = duplicate warning)

ol.li: Click Create
Enter address or use Google Places autocomplete
The system auto-geocodes and validates the address
Set location type (Warehouse / Customer / Relay / Rest Area / Fuel Station)
Upload entrance/dock photos for driver reference

div.div: A location that matches an existing one (same company + Google Place ID or address) will be flagged as a possible duplicate. Use the existing location instead unless this is genuinely a different entry.

div.p: Navigate: Network → FSAs / Regions / Cities

tr.td: Approved service area used by Corridors
Display label only (not used for pricing)
Ordered region on a weekly truck route

div.div: Cities are display-only. Region names must come from the approved LTL catalogue. New regions remain customer-hidden until their FSA coverage and map anchor are reviewed.

div.p: Navigate: Network → Corridors / Departures / Daily Local Operations

A Corridor is the single authority for a scheduled route: ordered regions, weekly days, start time, default truck, road distance, customer $/km, planned pallets, and future departures. Reverse direction requires a separate paired corridor unless the route is explicitly a same-day return.

tr.td: Hub → Niagara Region → Hamilton, Halton and Brant → Greater Toronto Area → York → Durham → Headwaters → Waterloo and Wellington regions → Hub
Hub → Durham → Northumberland → Southeastern Ontario → Montérégie → Laval → Centre-du-Québec → Québec, city and area → Chaudière-Appalaches → Bas-Saint-Laurent
Tuesday regions in reverse travel order → Hub
Hub → Northumberland → Southeastern Ontario → Ottawa Region → Haliburton Highlands to the Ottawa Valley → Kawarthas → Hub
Half-day Friday-pickup delivery or Monday-route carryover when assigned

div.p: Each stop on a corridor has: sequence, region, pickup/delivery/transfer permission, planned arrival/departure offsets, service duration, distance from origin, customer-visibility flag.

A Departure is one exact execution of a Corridor. The system maintains an eight-week rolling horizon. The Corridor's start time and default truck populate each new departure. Open one Departure only when a specific date needs a different truck. Changing weekly days removes/rebuilds only future unbooked Scheduled rows; booked or completed history is preserved.
Open any departure date to override just that execution:

ul.li: Change the Truck — the field shows Corridor Default when it matches the corridor's truck, or Departure Override for any other truck. New departures always inherit the default.
When the truck changes, the truck's assigned driver is attached automatically. A truck with no driver blocks the change — select a driver explicitly. Never leave a departure driver-less.
Capacity guard: the replacement truck must physically carry the pallets already reserved on that departure — reassignment is refused otherwise.
Truck reassignment is restricted to dispatch/operations management roles only.
Every change is recorded on the departure chatter: "Truck reassigned A → B", "Driver reassigned A → B", with the user and timestamp.
All LTL Planner jobs for that departure update to the new truck automatically.

div.div: Use this flow operationally when a truck breaks down: reassign the truck and driver on every affected departure date; booked capacity is re-validated against the replacement truck's layout automatically.

div.p: Navigate: Network → Where We Go
Where We Go is the authenticated network map. It shows configured direct and Hub-transfer destinations without exposing customer prices.

ul.li: Select a pickup point to draw lines to every reachable region marker
Select a destination to highlight its direct path or Pickup → YYZ-HUB → Destination transfer
Show the nearest exact departure; configured routes without one say “No bookable departure currently scheduled”
Never display price

tr.td: Try next departure or offer custom quote

div.p: The NetworkAvailabilityService queries real corridor/departure data including:

ul.li: Reserved pallets per departure (live booking data)
Vehicle capacity (assigned truck's layout — straight/pinwheel)
Temperature compatibility (Dry vs Reefer vehicle assignment)
Corridor stop sequences and region coverage

div.p: Every corridor stop carries a planned arrival/departure time computed from the departure's start time and the road distances between stops. The system shows the pickup and delivery ETA on quotes, bookings, and the live board — no manual ETA entry needed.

The calendar, Get Price, and the booking confirmation resolve the route with the same strict logic: pickup → hub-transfer → delivery legs with direction-aware transfer stops. A transfer shown in Where We Go is exactly the transfer priced in the quote and created on the booking — the portal can never show one route and book another. Corridors reachable only via a hub are correctly marked as transfer (never sold as direct), and exact departures are bound to each leg end-to-end.
div.div: Map reachability, booking route resolution, pricing, and departure selection use the same Corridor topology.

div.p: Navigate: Fleet → Trucks (list)

Each truck's list row shows its weekly day sequence (Monday → Sunday) with the corridor service configured for each day. This is a planning display only — it mirrors the weekly plan (e.g. Monday Southwestern Ontario, Tuesday eastbound, Wednesday westbound, Thursday HHB–Niagara, Friday southeastern) and has zero scheduling impact.

ul.li: The list is ordered Monday → Sunday so the week's plan reads top to bottom
Actual assignments are always made on the Dispatch Planner / exact Departures — the sequence view never books, reserves, or moves anything
A corridor archived or retired simply disappears from the sequence; the display never re-creates it

div.p: Navigate: Network → Service Routes (Corridors)

p.b: Customer $/km per pallet = Corridor $/km ÷ Planned Pallets
Booking price = Pallets × travelled road km × Customer $/km per pallet
Full-Corridor Revenue Target = Full Corridor Distance × Corridor $/km

div.p: The minimum booking charge is applied once to the complete booking, never once per transfer leg. Hub transfers add the priced pickup-to-Hub leg and Hub-to-delivery leg before applying the minimum.
div.h3: FTL Is Billed on Actual Road Distance
div.p: Full Truckload / dedicated quotes are billed on the actual door-to-door road distance — the real point-to-point driving distance between the pickup and delivery coordinates (Google Directions; straight-line × 1.4 when no driving route resolves). It is not the scheduled corridor segment distance:

ul.li: Pickup/delivery addresses with valid coordinates → actual measured distance × FTL $/km
Coordinates unavailable (postal-only quote) → scheduled corridor segment distance, clearly flagged
Multi-stop FTL: base is the FTL rate to the furthest destination, plus a per-stop surcharge ($50 same-region, $75 regional)
Single-stop FTL prints one frozen Dedicated FTL Transportation line at the final price — never recalculated
LTL keeps the scheduled corridor segment distance: the scheduled route is the LTL billable basis

div.p: Corridor pricing = what the customer pays. Prema AI Estimator = internal cost and NET PROFIT. These are never mixed or shown on Where We Go. Rate Plans and technical lanes remain readable only for historical bookings.
Every booking follows the same path regardless of how it enters the system:

ol.li: Customer Request — from any channel
Normalized Booking Request — all channels produce the same structure
Route Resolution — verified address/FSA → Region → Corridor(s) → exact Departure(s)
Pricing — Corridor formula for Scheduled LTL; explicit agreed rate for Custom/Expedited
Tax Decision — destination province → correct HST/GST
Capacity Check — per-segment pallet/weight validation with row locking
Booking Confirmation — one atomic transaction creates: Booking + Stops + Lines + Legs + Tax Snapshot + Invoice + Dispatch Job

div.div: Idempotency: Every booking has a unique idempotency key. Clicking "Confirm" twice, running the recurring cron twice, or approving a WhatsApp negotiation twice will NOT create duplicate bookings, invoices, or dispatch jobs.

div.p: Route: /my/booking (customer logs into their account)

ol.li: Customer selects pickup and delivery saved locations (multi-stop: add up to 20 delivery stops)
Customer enters Total Physical Pallets and per-stop allocation (dedicated or shared mode)
System resolves FSAs → Regions → Lanes → available departures and prices
Customer picks a pickup date from the eligible-date calendar
Customer reviews the quote: physical pallet count, per-stop breakdown, price
Customer confirms — system creates pricing session (20-min TTL)
On confirmation: Booking + Stops + Lines + Legs + Tax + Draft Invoice + Dispatch Job with physical pallet items

div.div: Portal bookings require the customer to have Logistics Pricing Status = Approved and be in the Logistics Customer group. See Section 22a — Physical Pallet & Stop Allocation for dedicated vs. shared pallet workflows.

div.p: Navigate: Bookings → Phone Booking

ol.li: Select Customer
Enter Pickup Postal Code and Delivery Postal Code
Enter Pallets, Weight (lbs), Temperature Mode (Dry/Reefer)
Optionally enter the Requested Pickup Date the customer asked for
Click Get Price — system shows lane, service, pickup date, delivery date, price
Click Confirm Booking — creates booking with tax, invoice, dispatch job

ul.li: When the customer's requested pickup date matches a bookable departure, that date is quoted and used

When the requested date has no bookable departure (no corridor runs that day, or the departure is full), the system offers the closest alternate date(s) with spare capacity — the dispatcher confirms which date with the customer
The exact departure chosen is bound to the booking at confirmation — capacity is reserved on that departure, never on a different one
FTL phone quotes quote and reserve the departure the same way, and bill on actual road distance (see §7)

div.div: Double-click safe: Clicking Confirm twice returns the same booking. No duplicate will be created.

div.p: Navigate: Bookings → All Bookings → Create

ol.li: Select Customer
Add Pickup Stops and Delivery Stops (with postal codes, addresses, contacts)
Set Pallets, Weight, Equipment Type (Dry/Reefer), Temperature
Choose Scheduled Network or Custom / Expedited
Scheduled Network uses Corridor pricing and exact departures. Custom / Expedited uses an explicit agreed rate.
Click Confirm — booking created with all linked records

div.div: Internal users can see both Customer Price and Internal Cost/NET PROFIT. This information is never visible to customers.

div.p: Navigate: Open any Draft Invoice → click Create/Open Booking

ol.li: System checks if a Booking already exists for this invoice
If it exists: opens the existing Booking (no duplicate)
If not: the Book Load wizard collects service type, saved pickup/delivery locations, pallets, weight, Dry/Reefer, temperature, and requested date
Scheduled LTL uses Corridor pricing and exact departures; Custom / Expedited uses the explicit invoice workflow
The existing draft invoice is linked and its freight amount uses the frozen booking price
One Planner operation card is created per physical truck/day; booking does not auto-dispatch the driver

div.div: Repeated clicks safe: Clicking Create/Open Booking twice opens the same booking. No duplicate invoice or dispatch job.
Historical invoices with existing dispatch jobs remain unchanged. Only new bookings use the V4 workflow.

div.p: Navigate: Bookings → WhatsApp Negotiations

ol.li: Customer sends load tender (PDF/image) via WhatsApp
System AI-extracts: stops, pallets, weight, commodity, pickup times
System runs Prema AI Estimator for internal cost
Staff reviews and negotiates rate via WhatsApp (interactive buttons)
Customer agrees on rate

Staff clicks Create Booking — system creates complete booking with:
Correct freight tax by destination province
Draft invoice with proper tax line
Dispatch job linked to booking and invoice

div.div: Internal cost is NEVER sent to the customer. WhatsApp replies show only: agreed rate, pickup/delivery, route description. Internal cost, NET PROFIT, and margin are hidden.

div.p: Navigate: Bookings → Custom Quotes
For unsupported destinations or special requests that don't match a standard corridor/lane.

ol.li: Create a new quote with: customer, pickup/delivery addresses, pallets, weight, equipment
Set quoted price manually
State flow: Draft → Reviewing → Quoted → Accepted/Declined → Converted
When Accepted: click Convert to Booking — creates complete booking through canonical service

ul.li: Click Print Quotation (available once a price is set) — renders a US-Letter PDF with the company letterhead
The document shows: quote number, issued/valid-until dates (30 days validity), status, shipment details, pickup/delivery addresses, the quoted freight charge, assigned departure, and terms
FTL quotations carry the actual-distance billing note (§7)

ol.li: Pick the Departure on the quote, then Convert — one booking is created, confirmed at the agreed price
The booking gets real pickup/delivery stops, one reserved leg on the chosen departure, and a DISP job card
A draft invoice is created at the quoted price (tax-inclusive; HST/GST split per destination)
Conversion is idempotent — clicking Convert twice returns the same booking, never a duplicate
The booking counts against the departure's capacity like any other (see §16)

div.p: Navigate: Bookings → Recurring Agreements
One customer agreement may contain up to 10 independent recurring jobs.

ol.li: Create the agreement with customer, contract/PO, start/end dates, billing notes, and service notes
Add each recurring job with a Region or Google-verified pickup and delivery address, frequency, weekday, windows, pallets, weight, Dry/Reefer, temperature, commodity, and accessorials
Region-only jobs may be tracked for planning; automatic booking requires both exact addresses to be Google verified
The daily cron generates due bookings through the same Corridor pricing and booking service
Each generated booking uses an idempotency key containing the recurring job and date
Running the cron twice creates no duplicates

div.div: The next shipment date advances only after successful booking creation. Failures create administrator activities (not silently swallowed).

div.p: Capacity is calculated per corridor segment, not per total truck. For each adjacent stop pair on a corridor, the system sums pallets and weight from all active bookings whose pickup is at or before that point and delivery is after it.

tr.td: Override Required — dispatcher must enable capacity override and provide reason

div.p: When a booking is confirmed, the system locks the corridor departure row (PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE), recalculates all active reservations, validates the proposed booking against per-segment limits, and commits atomically. If any segment fails, the entire booking rolls back — no partial reservations.
div.h3: Every Booking Counts — Including Manual and Phone

ul.li: Portal, phone, internal, custom-quote, and recurring bookings all reserve capacity on their departure the same way

Manual/negotiated bookings without a frozen route are anchored by their pickup/delivery FSA regions (canonicalized against the corridor's official region set), so they count in the departure's peak pallets and in the planner
FTL / dedicated bookings hold the entire truck — no LTL load can join an exclusively held departure

If a booking's regions don't fit the departure's corridor span (wrong direction, delivery beyond the route), the system flags an integrity conflict and refuses further bookings until it is corrected — a booking can never be silently uncounted
Cancelled bookings drop out of the peak immediately

div.div: Payload weight limit is always enforced independently of pallet count.

div.p: Navigate: Settings → Prema Logistics → Freight Tax Configuration
Tax is determined by the final delivery destination province and the customer's Billing Relationship.

tr.td: AB, BC, MB, SK, NT, YT, NU

div.p: If a required tax mapping is not configured:

ul.li: tax_review_required = True on the booking
Invoice stays Draft — cannot be posted or sent
An Accounting Review activity is created
A visible red banner appears on the booking form

div.div: Invoice posting is BLOCKED until the tax configuration is resolved. This prevents silently issuing tax-free invoices.

div.p: Navigate: Dispatch Operations → Booking Board
The primary board for ALL customer shipments regardless of entry channel. Shows every confirmed booking with:

ul.li: Source badge — Portal / Phone / Internal / Invoice / WhatsApp / Quote / Recurring
Booking number, Customer, Status (confirmed/planned/in_execution/delivered/completed/cancelled/exception)
Pickup, Delivery, Route, Departure
Pallets, Weight, Temperature
Tax review warning, Capacity status
Invoice status, Dispatch status, Truck, Driver

div.p: Clicking any card opens the canonical Booking form.
Navigate: Network → Service Routes → open a Corridor → Departures
Every active weekly Corridor maintains up to eight weeks of exact future departures. The separate Weekly Schedule board was removed because Dispatch Planner is the operational calendar.

ul.li: Default truck and start time come from the Corridor
Open a specific Departure to override its truck without changing other weeks
Capacity comes from that exact truck's verified layout and payload
A truck cannot hold another Corridor or custom job on the same operating day
Future booked departures and completed history are never deleted by a schedule change

div.p: A pickup on the day before a linehaul departure (e.g. Sunday pickup for Monday's run) is executed as one departure + one capacity pool: the freight is picked up on the prior day, held overnight, and rides the scheduled linehaul the next morning. Capacity counts once — the pickup and the linehaul never double-book the truck.

ul.li: Prior-day pickups are a corridor-level capability, enabled per corridor

Prior-day pickup is enabled per corridor. When enabled, a customer may select a prior-day physical pickup (for example Sunday) for the corridor's next scheduled departure (for example Monday). Sunday is not a linehaul operating day and no Sunday departure is created.
During live execution, an early next-day pickup is a recommendation only, never forced travel (see §26b)

div.div: The same departure row carries both the prior-day pickup and the linehaul — one reservation, one capacity check.

div.p: Navigate: Dispatch Operations → Dispatch Planner
The single operational truck/day calendar for scheduled LTL and custom work.

ul.li: Weekly calendar with truck rows and day columns
Confirmed LTL automatically appears on the exact Departure truck
A Monday pickup and Tuesday delivery appear as separate operation cards; no stretched two-day line
Multiple customer loads may share the same exact LTL Departure until pallet or weight capacity is full
Drag custom/unassigned jobs only onto free truck/day slots
Changing a Departure truck synchronizes every Planner card on that Departure
Auto-creates Load Plans on assignment
Pallet Layout panel for floor positioning
Truck utilization and driver assignment
Cross-dock transfer handoff tracking

div.div: Live en-route re-optimization is deferred. Use the existing manual Optimize action after reviewing any new pickup.

div.p: Navigate: Dispatch Operations → Live Map (also the default home page)
Real-time map showing all operational vehicles with:

ul.li: Current GPS position (from GeoTab)
Last GPS update time / stale warning
Vehicle name, license plate, driver
Current dispatch job and customer
Active stops with sequence and status
PB38446 visible. DEMO-01 hidden (x_operational_logistics filter)

div.div: The map shows ALL operational vehicles even without active dispatch jobs. Vehicles without recent GPS show their last known position with a "stale" indicator.

div.p: Navigate: Dispatch Operations → Load Plans
Physical truck loading plans. One per vehicle per operating date.

ul.li: Straight (12) — default, lengthwise positions L1-L6, R1-R6
Pin-Wheel (13) — proposed when pallets exceed 12, requires dispatcher acknowledgment
Turned (14) — angled positions, requires four-way-entry pallets
Assign/Move/Swap/Unassign — position pallets on the truck floor
Validate — check layout for blocking issues
Confirm Loading — mark as loaded
Lock/Unlock — manager can lock plan (prevents edits), unlock requires reason
Transfer Handoff — move pallets between trucks at transfer hubs
Recommend Layout — AI-suggested positions (advisory only, never auto-applied)

div.p: Prema Dispatch distinguishes between physical pallets (actual handling units on the truck) and stop allocations (which pallet serves which delivery stop).
Each physical pallet is assigned to a single delivery stop. The system creates one prema.dispatch.item per physical pallet.
Example: 3 physical pallets → Stop 1 receives Pallet 1, Stop 2 receives Pallets 2-3.
One physical pallet carries freight for multiple delivery stops. The pallet stays onboard until all its assigned stops are delivered.
Example: 1 physical pallet → contains items for Healthy Planet, NOFRILLS, Foodland, Metro. Capacity counted as 1, not 4.
In the Driver App, a shared pallet shows as PALLET P001 — SHARED with per-stop item assignments. At each stop, only that stop's freight is unloaded.
div.div: Pricing: Shared pallets are priced as ONE physical pallet for the entire journey — never charged multiple times for serving multiple stops. Capacity reservation counts physical pallets, never per-stop totals.

ol.li: Customer enters Total Physical Pallets (e.g., 3)
For each delivery stop, enters how many pallets go to that stop
System auto-creates physical pallet units and assigns them
Capacity reservation = total physical pallets entered
Customer checks "Shared Pallet / Mixed Stops"
Enters 1 physical pallet (or more if multiple shared pallets)
Each delivery stop is linked to the shared pallet(s)
Step 3 review shows: "1 Physical Pallet · Shared Across N Stops"

div.p: Shared pallets occupy one floor position on the truck, same as dedicated pallets. The load_unit_type field (pallet / shared_pallet) determines position consumption.
Stop allocations are stored via prema.dispatch.pallet.stop.allocation — the same model used by the Load Plan for shared-skid handling. Max 5 stops per physical pallet.

ul.li: prema.dispatch.item — one physical handling unit (pallet or shared pallet). Fields: load_unit_type, shared_skid, consumes_floor_position, stop_allocation_ids
prema.dispatch.pallet.stop.allocation — many-to-many join: one pallet → many stops. unique(item, stop)
logistics.pricing.session — booking-layer fields: physical_pallets, shared_pallet_mode
logistics.booking — confirmed booking fields: physical_pallets, shared_pallet_mode

div.p: Navigate: Dispatch Operations → Driver Worksheets
Generated when: Truck assigned + Driver assigned + Stops complete.
Each worksheet is unique per: driver + vehicle + operation/date.
Shows: ordered stops, booking references, customer names, pallets, weight, temperature, PO numbers, pickup/delivery windows, transfer info, contact info, POD requirements.
div.div: Worksheets are idempotent — generating twice returns the same worksheet. Missing stops block creation.

div.p: Navigate: Fleet → Trucks / Drivers
Assign truck on dispatch job or via Dispatch Planner. System validates:

ul.li: Reefer capability (if temperature-controlled freight)
Liftgate availability
Pallet capacity (straight/pin-wheel/turned)
Payload weight capacity

div.div: Conflicts show warnings. Manager can override with a mandatory reason logged in the assignment history.
div.p: Driver must have x_is_driver = True on their contact record. System auto-creates driver chat channel.
Driver opens Driver App (/dispatch/driver). Sees scheduled stops for today. At pickup: confirms pallet count, weight, takes photo evidence. System updates booking status and custody records.
Freight moves from one truck to another at the hub. Cross-dock drop → custody transition → cross-dock pickup on next truck. System tracks chain of custody.
div.div: Customer sees "Transit Mississauga, ON" — internal hub details (exact address, cross-dock layout) are never exposed.
div.p: Driver arrives at delivery. App shows: address, contact, items, instructions. Driver confirms delivery with POD photo/signature. System updates booking to delivered.
POD collected through the Driver App: photos of delivered freight, recipient signature, timestamp, GPS stamp. Attached to dispatch stop and booking. Triggers booking completion workflow.

The corridor is the framework; the confirmed stops are the actual route. When a truck executes, the system builds the real route from the confirmed dispatch stops only — corridor endpoints nobody confirmed are never forced onto the truck (corridor extent trim).
div.h3: What Never Moves During Live Reoptimization

ul.li: Stops already completed, arrived, en route, or manually route-locked keep their relative order
Only unlocked pending stops are reordered — by scheduled time, with delivery first when a pickup and a delivery share the same window (unloading reduces onboard load)
Stop sequences are renumbered (10/20/30…) to the actual order

div.p: Set Start Position on the dispatch job: Auto (prior-day end → depot → hub), Depot, Hub, GPS (enter latitude/longitude manually), or Prior-Day End (last completed stop of this truck's previous day).

A pickup scheduled early the next day is a pre-positioning recommendation, logged on the job's Route Recommendation Log — it is never inserted as forced travel. Check Ignore Route Recommendation to dismiss.

ul.li: Completed/arrived stops use actual times; en-route stops hold their ETA and pass the delay forward; pending stops advance by drive + service minutes
Each stop shows Live ETA, Delay (min) (live ETA − scheduled), and ETA Source (scheduled / live / override)
Set ETA Override on a stop (job Stops list or stop form) — the override wins for that stop and delays propagate from there

div.p: Customers only ever see: Estimated Arrival → Updated ETA → In Transit → Out for Delivery → Delivered. Internal details (truck, driver, carrier, stops) are never part of customer status.

Open a booking → Execution & Subcontracting page → Generate Scenarios. The engine builds a bounded set (max 8 alternatives) and recommends; the dispatcher decides (choose one or ignore). The frozen customer price is never changed by execution costs.

tr.td: Auto bookable (or Carrier Acceptance Required when it uses a subcontractor)
Own fleet dedicated direct (frozen leg estimates / Prema AI estimator)
Carrier Acceptance Required or Carrier Rate Required
Manual Review — always the honest fallback

ul.li: Own fleet = the booking's frozen leg estimates (from pricing / Prema AI) — never invented
Subcontract BUY hierarchy: accepted offer → carrier lane rate card → configured market authority → CARRIER RATE REQUIRED (no invented profitability)
Hub/transfer cost is the configured flat amount per hub split

div.p: Estimated margin = customer revenue − execution cost. Below the configured minimum, the booking shows a Margin Below Target banner — a warning for dispatcher decision, never a hard block. Choose This Scenario freezes the Execution Snapshot (audit); later cost or carrier changes never rewrite it.

Navigate: Network → Carriers. A carrier is a Contact with Transport Carrier checked — no separate master file. Profile: status (Active / Inactive / Pending Compliance / Blocked), home region, equipment capabilities, service regions, max pallets/weight, cross-border capability, insurance expiry, notes, and derived performance (loads completed, on-time %, invoice variances, avg buy rate).

Navigate: Network → Carrier Lane Rates. One card per carrier + origin/destination region + equipment: flat rate or rate-per-km (with minimum charge), effective dates (open-ended = always effective), BUY detention terms (free minutes, rate per increment), and extra stop charge.
Navigate: Network → Carrier Offers. One negotiation per booking leg: Request Availability → Enter Negotiation → Accept / Decline / No Response / Expire / Cancel. Rules:

ul.li: ONE accepted offer per leg — accepting a second for the same leg is refused
Accepting sets the leg's execution mode, carrier and buy rate, creates the freight Purchase Order (§26e) and recomputes the booking margin
Declining un-chooses any scenario that depended on that carrier

div.div: Lane rates, offers, buy rates and margins are INTERNAL. They never appear on the customer portal, public tracking, or the driver app.

div.p: Accepting an offer creates a native Purchase Order marked Freight Subcontract — one PO per leg (idempotent; the same leg can never produce a second PO). The Rate Confirmation is the same document as the PO: no parallel financial system.
On the PO form, the freight banner offers:

ul.li: Send Rate Confirmation — native Odoo email flow
Print Rate Confirmation — the PDF renders for freight POs only; ordinary POs are untouched
Record Carrier Acceptance — method (phone/email/signed/portal), recorded by/at
Review Vendor Bill vs Accepted Rate — see §26f

div.p: The PO carries the frozen freight details (load number, pickup/delivery, windows, pallets, weight, equipment, temperature, agreed rate, detention terms, POD requirement) used by the Rate Confirmation PDF.

Subcontracted legs track their own external status (confirmed → en route → delivered → …) and collect POD through the same attachment flow as own-fleet legs. The PREMAFIRM truck/driver are not involved — the dispatch job shows a Subcontracted execution badge.

ol.li: The carrier performs and invoices the load
Record the vendor bill against the freight PO (native flow) — this is the one payable; nothing is duplicated

Review Vendor Bill vs Accepted Rate compares the posted bill amount against the accepted buy rate and writes the actual cost + invoice variance on the leg — flagged, never silently applied, never rewriting the accepted rate
The booking's Actuals show real cost/margin only once billed (estimated hub/detention costs never masquerade as actuals)

div.p: Carrier BUY detention (from lane-rate/offer terms) and customer SELL detention (approved detention items) are separate totals — never netted, never exposed across sides.
div.div: The customer invoice never shows carrier data, buy rates, or vendor bills.

div.p: If a hub departure is cancelled/completed while freight is still waiting on it: Detect Missed Connections flags the leg (connection exception). Custody is preserved — the shipment is never falsely marked delivered. The dispatcher reviews and either releases the exception or recommends the next departure for that freight (recommendation only; the dispatcher decides).
If a carrier declines after the fact, the dependent scenario is un-chosen and the booking's execution decision returns to the dispatcher.

Subcontracting a Canada → USA leg requires the configured authority (Settings → Technical → System Parameters → logistics.allow_cross_border_subcontract). Without it, cross-border subcontract scenarios show COMPLIANCE REVIEW REQUIRED and fall to Manual Review.
Booking confirmation auto-creates a Draft Invoice with:

ul.li: Correct freight product (Dry/Reefer, CA/US)
Correct tax line from the booking's tax decision
Booking number as origin reference
Deterministic description (pickup, delivery, pallets, weight, PO, reference)
Verify: price matches booking, tax matches destination province
If tax_review_required = True: cannot post — resolve tax config first
Booking amount_untaxed + amount_tax = amount_total MUST equal invoice totals

div.p: Posted invoices flow to standard Odoo accounting. Bank reconciliation via Plaid sync (Wise, TD). Auto-reconcile models for recurring payment patterns.
Route: /track
Customers track shipments using Booking Number + Tracking Token (both required).
Visible to customer: status, pickup/delivery cities, estimated delivery date.
Status vocabulary (single authority, §26b): Estimated Arrival → Updated ETA → In Transit → Out for Delivery → Delivered.
Never visible: internal cost, NET PROFIT, margin, GPS coordinates, driver personal details, internal hub addresses, carrier/subcontract details, vendor bills, other customers' records.
div.div: The tracking token is a high-entropy random string. A booking number alone reveals nothing. This prevents anyone from guessing sequential booking numbers to see other shipments.
